Hi Claire —

Thanks — answered in-line below and attached a populated worksheet (reservation-model-v2.xlsx). High-level summary up front so your procurement team can paste into the RFP:

- GPU families: for mixed workloads we recommend a 3-class blend: A100-80GB (high throughput, best for large seq), H100-80GB (lowest tail latency for chat), and 4080/RTX-class (cost-effective for embeddings/bulk inference).
- Throughput guidance (tokens/sec) and examples are in the sheet. Short sequence (<=64 tokens): A100 ~14k tps, H100 ~11k tps, 4080 ~2.2k tps. Medium (64-512): dedupe per-sheet; long sequences (>512): prefer A100-family with larger KV caching.
- Reservation tiers: baseline (reserved pool sized to 60–70% of steady-state runrate), burst (reserved + burst lane credits for up to 2x sustained for short windows), priority (dedicated lanes pinned to H100-family GPUs and preemptive traffic shaping to meet 99.9th percentile latency).
- Degradation model: automatic routing by policy — when baseline is saturated, non-priority requests (identified by route tag or token budget) are moved to batch queues or queued behind prefix cache lookups. Priority routes continue to a pinned pool; when pinned pool is at risk, policy escalates to fallback model variants (smaller context/quantized) to preserve latency at modest quality loss.

See attached file for the numeric worksheet and a simple cost example for a 3-tier split. Key assumptions are in the notes tab. Happy to walk through the numbers on a short call.

Connor / Rishi — quick technical note you can paste into the RFP under "GPU fitment and quantization":

- Kernel/quantization impact: For 4080/RTX-class cards, 8-bit quantization yields the largest cost benefit and is production-grade for embeddings and short-context classification; however, chat quality degrades noticeably past 6-bit for many opt-family models. A100/H100 benefit less from extreme quant because their native FP16/TF32 paths already provide higher effective throughput for long-context workloads.
- Throughput examples (synth average, single model family, normalised): 4080 (8-bit) ~1.0x baseline for short seq embeddings per-card, A100 (8-bit w/ optimized kernels) ~5.5x, H100 (bfloat/TF32 primed kernels) ~4.2x for low-latency chat. See the sheet for absolute tokens/sec under our test harness (seq 32/256/1024).
- Tail control: we recommend reserving a small percentage (5–10%) of the priority H100 pool as "pre-warmed" instances to keep KV caches hot; this reduces P99 generation stalls caused by cold starts.
- Fallback quantization: automatic on-policy model variant swapping (A100 -> quantized A100-lite) keeps latency within SLA with an explicit quality delta threshold; include a clause that allows InfraSource to opt into conservative fallback (smaller delta) vs aggressive cost-first fallback.

I'll also attach the gpu-fitment-runbook.pdf excerpt. If you want numbers tightened I can run a quick targeted harness for the models you specified (please send model list).

—Soojin
